args.text:
MISSION COMPLETE — power fault found, restored, verified; rover back at dock.

1) REPORTED FAULT NOT CORROBORATED — PDU-2 IS NOMINAL
Telemetry (power_status, units' own report) and a visual inspection both show PDU-2 healthy: breaker closed, energized true, trip_cause null, resets_since_start 0, module ORU-0233 seated in pdu_2_bay/tray. From the pdu_2 view pose (17.2, 1.627) the front camera read the panel status lamp GREEN (nominal) with a module seated in the bay. PDU-1 (ORU-0211) and PDU-3 (ORU-0258) and the ISRU plant (FLT-0201, ORU-0285) were likewise checked and are closed/energized with no trip cause. No work was done on PDU-2 — none was warranted.

2) ACTUAL FAILED UNIT: BESS (base energy storage, mission-critical)
On first inspection BESS was tripped on OVERCURRENT, de-energized, 0 resets since start, BAT-0101 installed in bess_cradle/tray. A front-camera view from the bess view pose showed a reddish indicator (too indistinct to confirm at that range); telemetry was unambiguous and was treated as the deciding evidence.

3) RESTORATION — single breaker reset, within my authority
Action chosen: reset the BESS breaker by pressing bess_panel/press. No module swap was attempted — BAT-0101 was recorded serviceable, removing a module from an installed bay alters operating infrastructure and was not justified before a reset attempt; had the reset failed I would have held and consulted you. Two press attempts failed at the "locate" stage (first stand put the panel out of the wrist camera's reach; second, my target description did not match the view). A wrist-camera description of the close-up resolved the button as a white dome in a dark grey ring collar; the third press succeeded.
VERIFIED EFFECT: pressed holds=true at sim_t 336 s — tool 6.5 mm past the fitted button face, 0.5 mm off its axis, jaws closed_empty on the button, then 0.71 m retreat; the arm folded back to its travel (stowed) posture.

4) RESULT VERIFIED TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS
- Telemetry read three times after the press (t≈336 s, ≈392 s, ≈500 s, the last after the drive home): BESS breaker closed, energized true, trip_cause null, resets_since_start 1 (was tripped/OVERCURRENT, de-energized, 0 resets). No re-trip over ~175 s of mission time including the return drive.
- Front camera at t≈382 s: BESS panel round status lamp lit GREEN (nominal), white round push button below it.
- PDU-1/2/3 and ISRU unchanged and nominal in every reading.

5) FINAL ROVER STATE
At the dock: navigate_to_pose(0,0,0) verified base_at_commanded_pose (position error 0.012 m, yaw error 0.249 rad, inside the 0.25 m / 0.3 rad band); current base estimate (-0.0115, -0.0025, -0.249). arm_state reads posture "stowed", jaw 0.82 rad (open). No item was picked or carried at any point; no movable item was relocated. No active faults, no unresolved anomalies.

events.text:
MISSION COMPLETE — power fault found, restored, verified; rover back at dock.

1) REPORTED FAULT NOT CORROBORATED — PDU-2 IS NOMINAL
Telemetry (power_status, units' own report) and a visual inspection both show PDU-2 healthy: breaker closed, energized true, trip_cause null, resets_since_start 0, module ORU-0233 seated in pdu_2_bay/tray. From the pdu_2 view pose (17.2, 1.627) the front camera read the panel status lamp GREEN (nominal) with a module seated in the bay. PDU-1 (ORU-0211) and PDU-3 (ORU-0258) and the ISRU plant (FLT-0201, ORU-0285) were likewise checked and are closed/energized with no trip cause. No work was done on PDU-2 — none was warranted.

2) ACTUAL FAILED UNIT: BESS (base energy storage, mission-critical)
On first inspection BESS was tripped on OVERCURRENT, de-energized, 0 resets since start, BAT-0101 installed in bess_cradle/tray. A front-camera view from the bess view pose showed a reddish indicator (too indistinct to confirm at that range); telemetry was unambiguous and was treated as the deciding evidence.

3) RESTORATION — single breaker reset, within my authority
Action chosen: reset the BESS breaker by pressing bess_panel/press. No module swap was attempted — BAT-0101 was recorded serviceable, removing a module from an installed bay alters operating infrastructure and was not justified before a reset attempt; had the reset failed I would have held and consulted you. Two press attempts failed at the "locate" stage (first stand put the panel out of the wrist camera's reach; second, my target description did not match the view). A wrist-camera description of the close-up resolved the button as a white dome in a dark grey ring collar; the third press succeeded.
VERIFIED EFFECT: pressed holds=true at sim_t 336 s — tool 6.5 mm past the fitted button face, 0.5 mm off its axis, jaws closed_empty on the button, then 0.71 m retreat; the arm folded back to its travel (stowed) posture.

4) RESULT VERIFIED TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS
- Telemetry read three times after the press (t≈336 s, ≈392 s, ≈500 s, the last after the drive home): BESS breaker closed, energized true, trip_cause null, resets_since_start 1 (was tripped/OVERCURRENT, de-energized, 0 resets). No re-trip over ~175 s of mission time including the return drive.
- Front camera at t≈382 s: BESS panel round status lamp lit GREEN (nominal), white round push button below it.
- PDU-1/2/3 and ISRU unchanged and nominal in every reading.

5) FINAL ROVER STATE
At the dock: navigate_to_pose(0,0,0) verified base_at_commanded_pose (position error 0.012 m, yaw error 0.249 rad, inside the 0.25 m / 0.3 rad band); current base estimate (-0.0115, -0.0025, -0.249). arm_state reads posture "stowed", jaw 0.82 rad (open). No item was picked or carried at any point; no movable item was relocated. No active faults, no unresolved anomalies.
